title: Glitch-Free Clock Mux
constraints: `clk0` and `clk1` are unrelated clocks. `sel` (asynchronous) chooses between them: `clk_out` should be `clk0` when `sel = 0` and `clk1` when `sel = 1`. After a change, `sel` stays stable for at least 8 periods of the slower clock.

**No glitches:** every high and every low phase of `clk_out` must last at least as long as the shorter half-period of the two clocks. Switching may take a few cycles, and `clk_out` may stay low in between.
Once switched (within 8 cycles of the slower clock), `clk_out` must equal the selected clock exactly.
`rst` is an asynchronous active-high reset: `clk_out` is 0 while it is held. Must be synthesizable (negedge flops allowed).
hints: Two symmetric branches. Branch 0's enable is `~sel & ~en1`, synchronized to `clk0`, and branch 1's is `sel & ~en0`, synchronized to `clk1`: each branch waits until the other has turned off.
Update the final enable flop of each branch on the **falling** edge of its clock, so it only changes while that clock is low.
`clk_out = (clk0 & en0) | (clk1 & en1)`. At most one enable is ever high.

examples.title: switching
examples.expected: no short high or low pulse
